text:
Ingrid: heads-up — ran the overnight perf sweep on the int8 kv cache profile for the longctx workload. seeing steady memory growth + slot fragmentation after ~45k tokens, even when eviction is enabled.

Alex: can you paste the profiler output? is this only on int8 or also bf16/fp16?

Ingrid: here are the key numbers from the run (summarized):
PerfBot: summary -> model: redwood-phi-13b-int8, workload: longctx-100k, runtime: 6h, peak-rss: 28.2GB, kv-allocs: 12.3k, kv-frag-ratio: 0.37, kv-evictions: 1.2k, steady-growth-rate: ~0.5MB/min.

Tj: hmm frag ratio 0.37 is pretty high. was compaction triggered?

Ingrid: compaction is on at 60s intervals. but the compaction pass doesn't reduce RSS much — suggests many small holes rather than big contiguous pages.

Keisha: is kernel selection different for int8 paths? we switched a couple of kernels to the quant-optimized codegen last month — maybe allocation size/align changed.

Alex: good point. if the int8 execution path switches to a tiled kernel that allocs slightly different KV slabs per layer/seq-len, fragmentation can accumulate over long sequences. worth checking allocation site shapes.

Ingrid: attached snippet from jemalloc stats at the end of the run:
```
active: 25.9GB
mapped: 30.4GB
allocated_objects: 62340
small_allocs: 49210
large_allocs: 13130
slab_waste_est: 1.8GB
internal_frag_bytes: 9.6GB
```

Tj: internal_frag_bytes 9.6GB aligns with the frag ratio. two hypotheses: (1) int8 per-token KV grows smaller sized objects that don't coalesce, (2) eviction heuristics aren't aggressive enough for longctx streaming.

PerfBot: patch-check -> top 3 hot alloc callsites (addr truncated):
- runtime/kv_cache.cc:123 allocate_slot(size=4096) count=41.2k
- runtime/batching.cc:87 allocate_batch_buffer(size=8192) count=12.9k
- kernels/int8/attention.cc:301 temp_buf(size=2048) count=58.1k

Keisha: attention temp_buf churn looks suspicious. those temp buffers should be arena-backed and ephemeral, not persistent in the kv slab. are we accidentally pinning them to the slab allocator used for KV?

Glen: i noticed a recent change in the allocator wrapper: we started reusing the global allocator for some quant kernels to reduce malloc overhead. that could mix lifetimes.

Alex: action item: audit allocator scopes in int8 kernels. if temp buffers use the KV slab arena, move them to thread-local scratch or stack where possible.

Ingrid: also ran a quick A/B with bf16 on same workload: bf16 peak-rss 33.1GB but frag ratio only 0.12 and steady-growth negligible. int8 saved memory overall but fragmented badly.

Tj: so tradeoff: int8 reduces raw footprint but increases internal fragmentation and long-term growth. we need strategies to keep both benefits.

Keisha: ideas: (a) adjust eviction to evict oldest slots earlier for longctx, (b) run a proactive compaction pass when fragmentation crosses threshold, (c) change allocator alignment to unify small alloc sizes, (d) kernel-level change: avoid allocating temps into KV arena.

Alex: i'd prioritize kernel/allocator fix first — it's lower risk and addresses root cause. if allocator change isn't sufficient, follow up with eviction policy tuning.

Glen: proposing an experiment plan:
1) revert allocator wrapper change in a canary build (bench + overnight longctx run). 2) instrument per-callsite allocator tag so we can tell which subsystems are using KV arenas. 3) run compaction-disabled vs compaction-every-10s to measure effectiveness.

Ingrid: i'll run the canary tonight. leaving the profiler hooks enabled and adding new telemetry: `kv.alloc_tag`, `kv.slot_age_hist`, `kv.frag_pct_by_size_bucket`.

PerfBot: perf-run scheduled -> job id: pr-4821-longctx-canary, ETA complete: 8h. will post results in thread.

Keisha: small config snippet if we want to try a softer but more aggressive eviction policy temporarily:
```
kv.eviction.min_free_percent = 8
kv.eviction.age_threshold_secs = 120
kv.compaction.force_on_threshold = 0.28
```

Tj: one more thought — batching heuristics interacting with quant kernels could increase simultaneous live KV slots. e.g., larger batch windows for int8 make more slots simultaneously resident. worth checking batch size distribution in the logs.

Alex: please add `batch.window_hist` to telemetry too.

Ingrid: noted. i'll post the canary output and perfbot summary tomorrow. thanks all. :wave:

Glen: :thumbsup: if the allocator revert fixes fragmentation we can roll to dedicated for canary traffic and schedule a papering of the kernel change.

PerfBot: update -> pr-4821-longctx-canary completed, results posted at 1875550345. metrics show frag ratio dropped from 0.37 -> 0.09 and peak-rss reduced by 2.1GB after allocator revert. full logs: https://perf.redwood/internal/pr-4821/output

Ingrid: great signal. i'll open a follow-up to move temp buffers out of KV arena and add alloc tags.

Keisha: thanks. i'll prepare an A/B with the adjusted eviction config after the kernel fix.

Alex: nice work team. small next steps in GH: audit, patch, canary, telemetry.

Tj: and we'll keep an eye on accuracy — quant regressions popped up before when changing kernels. run the evals in parallel.

Ingrid: will do. closing loop once the eval results are in.
